prose.text:  AI text generation and structured reasoning for learner-facing and admin-facing functions.  Provider adapters for cloud free tiers, local models and optional paid providers later.  AI conversation and role-play in text; voice mode through existing STT/TTS/speech adapters when enabled.  Personalized explanation, adaptive hinting, writing feedback and additional practice generation.  Admin-assisted content drafting, QA suggestions, metadata completion, media prompt/script generation, analytics summaries and controlled low-risk automation.  AI settings, provider routing, feature flags, quotas, audit, privacy classification, safety checks and evals. 1.2. Поза межами цього baseline

 Autonomous AI publication of curriculum without human editorial gates.  AI deletion of user accounts, role changes, billing changes or irreversible production operations.  Live image/audio generation as a dependency of ordinary lesson completion.  Using model output as official CEFR certification or as unvalidated high-stakes assessment.  Permanent storage of hidden model reasoning/chain-of-thought. Only final outputs, structured traces and policy metadata needed for operation may be stored.  Assumption that any specific free provider or model will remain free indefinitely.

Core product invariant: if every AI provider is disabled, rate-limited or offline, the user must still be able to log in, open published lessons, complete deterministic exercises, receive normal feedback, save progress, use Review, collections, audio assets and resume learning.
The system MUST not assume one permanent AI vendor. Provider selection is configuration, not product identity. Start policy is free/local-first with hard protection against accidental paid usage.
Start default: paid_inference_enabled = false; monthly_paid_budget = 0; free_only = true. Exhausting a free quota disables/falls back the AI capability. It MUST NOT silently switch to a paid model.

Entry point examples: "Пояснити інакше", "Чому тут так?", "Дай ще один приклад". AI receives the current knowledge_item, approved explanation/usage notes, target language/variety, CEFR scope and minimal mistake context. It explains in uk-UA by default and must stay within the learner level unless explicitly asked to extend.

AI may choose or phrase a hint only within the activity hint_policy. It MUST NOT expose the full answer before reveal is allowed. Hint usage remains assistance evidence and affects scheduling according to the existing deterministic rules. 7.3. Extra practice generator

AI feedback should separate: task completion, meaning, grammar/form, vocabulary/chunks, register, spelling/punctuation and suggested rewrite. The learner original is preserved according to privacy policy. A polished rewrite must be clearly marked as a suggestion, not silently substituted for the learner response.  For A1/A2, use short, concrete feedback and one or two highest-value corrections.  For B1-C1, allow richer rubric feedback, register and cohesion comments.  AI writing score is not authoritative mastery unless a calibrated rubric/evaluator version is approved.
The model must not rely on its general memory as curricular truth when Lingvessa already has approved content. The Grounding Builder assembles only the context needed for the request.

Lingvessa retains the two-level mastery model fixed in Technical Design v1.7: six global skill projections (Vocabulary, Grammar, Listening, Speaking, Writing, Pronunciation) plus the canonical knowledge-item facet registry (e.g. recognition, meaning, recall_l2_to_l1, recall_l1_to_l2, production, spelling, orthography, listening_recognition/listening_gist/listening_detail, pronunciation_target, intelligibility, context_use, collocation, grammar_form, word_order, morphology, register, variant_awareness, interaction_repair, interaction_goal). Every evidence target must use an allowed skill-facet pair.

 AI-generated correction distinguishes learner original, correction and explanation.  Conversation offers correction intensity/mode and text/voice availability according to capability.  AI never hides the ordinary Reveal/Retry/Continue rules of scored core activities.  Accessibility: keyboard, screen-reader status, reduced motion, captions/transcripts and non-mic alternatives remain available. 17.2. Admin UX

 Global AI enabled toggle plus separate Learning AI and Admin AI toggles.  Mode selector Manual / AI Assist / AI Auto.  Per-capability switches and risk labels.  Provider/model priority, free-only setting, quota and budget dashboard.  Data-policy eligibility visible for learner vs admin tasks.  Proposal diff before Apply; audit link after action.  One-click emergency disable for provider and for all AI.

EU launch note: AI interaction should be transparently identified to users, and Article 50 AI Act obligations must be evaluated per flow/provider/deployer role. The platform should not rely on users guessing that a conversational partner is artificial.

 Two-level mastery model remains authoritative; AI does not collapse skills/facets.  Speech contract from Technical Design v1.7 remains: usable speech may show correct/try again; unavailable/low- confidence neutral and non-blocking.  AI-generated images/audio for course content are pre-generated through Media Pipeline, QA-reviewed and versioned before publish.  No provider free tier is assumed permanent. 22.2. ADRs required later

 AI provider/domain ports, policy engine, budget controls, prompt registry and audit contracts are versioned and tested.  At least one local/free adapter can be enabled without changing learner/admin feature contracts.  Paid inference is provably blocked under default configuration.  English and Czech reference fixtures pass AI explanation/hint bilingual evals and provider-offline fallback tests.  AI-generated learner practice cannot silently inflate mastery.  Admin AI cannot publish or execute privileged/destructive commands.  All AI Auto actions are allowlisted, draft-scoped, diffable and audited.  Outbound payload privacy allowlists and provider data-policy registry are active.  No secrets, raw chain-of-thought or raw microphone bytes appear in AI logs/analytics.  AI UX is labeled, accessible and has non-AI alternatives.  Provider/model/prompt/policy versions appear in diagnostics and eval reports.  Incident controls can disable provider or all AI without redeploy and without breaking core learning.  Governing Formal/Technical/Curriculum/Reference documents are synchronized in the next controlled revisions.
This appendix is operational guidance, not a permanent vendor commitment. Free limits and data policies can change; every provider profile MUST be revalidated before enabling it in production.

Precedence: Formal controls product/pedagogical scope; Curriculum controls A1 pedagogy; Technical Specification controls normative technical requirements; Technical Design controls concrete implementation detail; AI Specification controls AI-specific behavior; Reference Module Design is the executable fixture; Implementation Plan controls execution order only. Any unresolved conflict blocks implementation until an owner decision and controlled revision/ADR.
Canonical identity and version contract

API/JSON examples MUST use UUID-shaped values in *_id fields. Content manifests MAY use stable_code for authoring references, but the build/publish step resolves them to UUID + version_code and rejects unresolved codes.
Canonical AI API and persistence mapping

Learner AI is OFF by default. Effective enablement order: global AI flag -> capability flag -> approved provider/model/data policy -> learner opt-in and required consent -> quota/budget. Any failed check returns deterministic fallback; no paid fallback is implicit.

1. Призначення, межі та нормативність Blueprint переводить продуктову й технічну специфікації Lingvessa у навчальну архітектуру A1. Він визначає, що користувач має вміти, у якій послідовності розвиваються знання й уміння, які докази приймаються для mastery та які артефакти потрібні для production. Це не збірник готових уроків і не обіцянка автоматичної зовнішньої сертифікації CEFR. Ключове рішення English і Čeština є двома стартовими target languages. Вони використовують спільні Lesson Engine, Review Engine, Mastery Engine, Media Pipeline та optional AI capability layer, але мають окремі curriculum versions, language profiles, progress, mastery/review state і language-specific pedagogy. Review або AI context однієї мови не може випадково змішуватися з іншою. • Усі модулі, examples, dialogues, explanations, activities, visual assets і audio scripts мають бути оригінальними або належно ліцензованими; не копіювати Babbel чи інший комерційний курс. • Навчальна ціль формулюється як реальна дія користувача (can-do); граматика, лексика, pronunciation і strategy є засобами цієї дії. • Кожен module завершується Module Recap у новій ситуації. Recap не є повтором тих самих screens. • Optional A1 Level Test оцінює внутрішню readiness і не блокує доступ до A2. • AI є optional learner assistance/practice. Відсутність AI не блокує lesson, recap, review, Level Test або progression. Нормативні слова MUST - обов’язково для приймання; SHOULD - очікувана практика, відхилення потребує обґрунтування; MAY - дозволений варіант. При конфлікті діє пізніше зафіксоване рішення власника продукту; документ оновлюється controlled revision. 2. A1 exit profile та CEFR alignment A1 у Lingvessa є збалансованим профілем, а не одним сумарним балом. Course completion означає проходження content path; A1 readiness означає достатній внутрішній evidence profile; зовнішній сертифікат може видати лише уповноважена екзаменаційна організація.

Обов’язкова послідовність сенсу Context -> input/noticing -> concise Ukrainian explanation -> controlled practice -> active retrieval -> listening/communication -> result/remediation. Не кожен screen реалізує всі стадії, але lesson як ціле MUST мати context, active retrieval і visible result.
Core guarantee AI disabled, unavailable, rate-limited or out of free quota must not block core lesson, Recap, Review, Level Test or course progression. The non-AI path remains complete.

• Evaluation accepts meaningful en-GB/en-US variants by activity configuration; it does not silently mix voice varieties. • Contractions and uncontracted forms are knowledge-aware variants, not blanket string normalization. • Pronunciation usable evidence may show correct/try again; unavailable speech is neutral and never the only completion route. • Every required media object is pre-generated, versioned and linked by asset_id before publish. • AI support in M01 is optional and must use approved E-A1-M01 knowledge/content as grounding.

• Missing diacritic may be a form/orthography error without erasing meaning evidence. • Accepted word order is pattern-aware; evaluator does not reduce Czech to English token order. • Formal/informal address is explicit content metadata. • Pronunciation focuses on intelligibility and salient contrast, not imitation of one speaker. • AI explanation/hints for Czech MUST ground on approved morphology/register rules and preserve cs-CZ forms.

Binary feedback, not binary gate A usable speech result MAY produce a simple learner-facing correct / try again state. It MUST NOT be treated as definitive language judgment when confidence is low. Mic denial, timeout, low confidence or provider failure become speech_unavailable and create no negative Speaking/Pronunciation evidence. Raw scores need not be shown. • Mic permission is requested just in time after explicit learner action; active recording may pulse/animate and MUST respect reduced-motion. • Correct pronunciation state may expose “Далі” or allow Auto-advance according to activity policy. • Try-again/error state gives a short target-feature cue when evaluator evidence is usable; retry and/or controlled continuation follow the activity contract. • AI may explain a structured target-feature issue only when the speech subsystem supplies usable evidence; AI does not invent a pronunciation diagnosis. 11.1. Slow audio and voices • Relevant word, sentence and dialogue players provide normal and slow playback with pitch preservation where technically possible. • A separately recorded slow asset MAY be used when playback-rate reduction distorts the pedagogical target. • Every audio asset stores language, variety, speaker/voice_id, script version, speed, rights/provenance and transcript. • Dialogues use multiple voices where roles differ; avatar, speaker label and voice_id stay synchronized. 12. Review, two-level mastery and spiral recycling

No invented pass mark Coverage and evidence are defined now; final readiness bands require pilot data, item analysis and expert review. AI-generated judgment or LLM confidence MUST NOT become the pass threshold.

15. AI learning blueprint AI in Lingvessa A1 is a bounded, grounded extension of the curated curriculum. It does not replace the lesson sequence, the knowledge graph, deterministic answer policies or human-authored reference content. AI learner functions may be enabled per capability and must always expose a complete non-AI fallback.

• Grounding refs and exact content/knowledge versions are retained where relevant. • Learner context sent to AI is minimized; no broad export of account/history. • AI must preserve English variety, Czech morphology/diacritics/register and approved accepted variants. • If AI is contradictory, unavailable or uncertain, Lingvessa falls back to curated content instead of inventing a rule. • AI-generated content is not automatically published course content; published material continues through content QA workflow. ЧАСТИНА G. PRODUCTION GOVERNANCE 16. Content production gates

Architecture validation rule The two Reference Modules validate the shared contracts. If Czech content or learner AI requires an English-specific workaround rather than configuration/strategy within the common model, Technical Specification/Design must be revised before full A1 production. 18. Normative requirements and acceptance

Precedence: Formal controls product/pedagogical scope; Curriculum controls A1 pedagogy; Technical Specification controls normative technical requirements; Technical Design controls concrete implementation detail; AI Specification controls AI-specific behavior; Reference Module Design is the executable fixture; Implementation Plan controls execution order only. Any unresolved conflict blocks implementation until an owner decision and controlled revision/ADR. Canonical mastery/facet registry
Facet-to-global-skill aggregation

Reading is not a seventh global mastery skill. Reading tasks may emit item-facet evidence to Vocabulary and/or Grammar according to the objective. The optional Level Test may report a separate assessment_domain=reading subscore; that subscore is assessment-only and is not persisted as skill_mastery_states. Canonical identity and version contract

API/JSON examples MUST use UUID-shaped values in *_id fields. Content manifests MAY use stable_code for authoring references, but the build/publish step resolves them to UUID + version_code and rejects unresolved codes. Canonical pronunciation state and asynchronous speech-job contract
Canonical state names are speech_correct, speech_incorrect and speech_unavailable. Legacy labels speech_feedback_correct and speech_feedback_retry are invalid. speech_job lifecycle

created -> uploaded -> queued -> processing -> succeeded | unavailable | failed | cancelled | expired. POST /api/v1/speech/jobs with Idempotency-Key + attempt_id creates or returns the same owner/profile/item/content-bound job and returns job_id + single-use upload_url. PUT upload_url uploads encrypted transient audio; POST /api/v1/speech/jobs/{job_id}/submit queues scoring; GET /api/v1/speech/jobs/{job_id} returns owner-scoped status/result; POST /api/v1/speech/jobs/{job_id}/cancel idempotently settles speech_unavailable(reason=user_cancelled). Continue is the normal LessonPlayer Next action after a terminal speech outcome and creates no new attempt. succeeded maps exactly once to speech_correct/speech_incorrect using evidence_map; unavailable/failed/expired map exactly once to speech_unavailable after bounded retries. Network retries reuse attempt_id/idempotency/job; learner Retry after a terminal result creates a NEW attempt_id/job; signed late/duplicate callbacks after settlement are ignored; raw audio is deleted at terminal settlement/cancel or TTL <=15 minutes.

• Провести учня через context -> exposure/noticing -> concise explanation -> guided practice -> active retrieval -> communication -> remediation -> spaced review -> higher-level reuse. • Окремо відстежувати Vocabulary, Grammar, Listening, Speaking, Writing і Pronunciation, не зводячи навчання до одного відсотка. • На рівні конкретного knowledge item розрізняти meaning/recognition, productive recall, spelling, listening recognition, pronunciation, context use та релевантні language-specific facets. • Повернути слабкий і забутий матеріал у потрібний момент, у нових contexts і з поступовим зменшенням підказок. • Надати весь required learning content і media без обов’язку користувача самостійно шукати, фотографувати або створювати зображення чи аудіо. • Дозволити масштабувати рівні A1-C1, professional tracks та нові мови без переписування Lesson, Review, Mastery, Media та AI integration contracts. • Використовувати AI для персоналізації й адміністрування лише як керований capability layer, а не як dependency core course. 1.2. Ознаки успішної реалізації • Користувач перемикає English і Čeština, а progress/mastery/review/collections іншої мови не змінюються. • Одна activity-компонента відображає різний structured content без hardcoded lesson sentences у UI. • Після помилки система дає конкретний feedback, retry/reveal за policy, фіксує evidence і планує review. • Published item має knowledge/outcome mapping, accepted answer policy, feedback, accessibility fields і всі required media references. • Published content/assets versioned; rollback не втрачає progress і historical evidence. • При повністю вимкненому AI користувач може пройти published lessons, Review, collections, audio і зберегти progress. 2. Межі версії v1

Two-level mastery model 1) Six global skill projections: Vocabulary, Grammar, Listening, Speaking, Writing, Pronunciation. 2) Per-knowledge-item facets: recognition, meaning, production, spelling, listening_recognition, pronunciation, context_use and reviewed language-specific facets such as collocation, morphology, word_order, register. A single overall score MUST NOT hide missing facet coverage.

• Inputs: correctness, attempts, reveal, hints, response time, item difficulty, time since retrieval, error type, mastery/facet state. • Session: due first, then weak; limited new/recycle; interleaving; spacing between near-duplicates. • Skip is not success and does not postpone due date like correct retrieval. • Topic selection and personal collections can constrain what is reviewed, while scheduler still prioritizes weak/due items.

• Read aloud; Listen & Repeat; Role-play; dialogue playback by speaker. • Normal + slow playback; slow mode preserves pitch or uses reviewed slow asset. • Voice assets scoped en-GB/en-US/cs-CZ; multi-speaker dialogues bind voice_id/avatar/current audio state. • Microphone button begins recording only after explicit user action; while recording it visually pulses unless reduced- motion is active. • For usable/high-confidence speech, learner-facing result is simple correct or try again/incorrect; raw numeric score is not required in UI. • On correct, Next becomes available or Auto-advance may proceed according to setting. On incorrect, concise feedback and retry/continue behavior follow activity policy. • Mic denial, unsupported device, timeout, provider failure or low-confidence recognition => speech_unavailable; neutral, non-blocking, no negative Speaking/Pronunciation evidence. • Raw microphone audio is transient by default and not stored in logs/analytics/object storage without explicit separate policy.

• Create, rename, edit, archive/delete; add words, phrases, chunks, questions and useful sentences. • Play all audio and Review only this collection. • Collection entry links to knowledge/content entity when available; custom text stored separately. • Collection language is explicit; mixed-language collection is not created accidentally.

Lingvessa has one provider-agnostic AI Layer for learner-facing and admin-facing capabilities. AI improves explanation, practice, personalization and operations, but cannot replace curriculum, deterministic state machine, published content governance or learner evidence model. Core-without-AI invariant If every AI provider is disabled, rate-limited or offline, learner MUST still be able to log in, open published lessons, complete deterministic exercises, receive normal feedback, save progress, use Review, collections, audio assets and resume learning.

Target: WCAG 2.2 AA for learner-facing core flows, independent of legal applicability in launch country. • Keyboard navigation, visible focus, logical tab order, names/roles/states. • 200% zoom/reflow; core content from 320 CSS px without horizontal scroll. • Primary touch targets >= 44x44 CSS px; reduced motion; no information by colour alone. • Alt text/decorative markers; transcripts/captions; non-drag alternatives. • Mic pulse respects prefers-reduced-motion and is never sole recording state signal. • AI learner/admin UI must expose what is AI-generated where policy requires and have accessible non-AI fallback for core learning.

• Interface language; target language; English variety; goals; active course/track. • Auto-advance; normal/slow audio; captions/transcript; microphone controls. • Learner AI enable/disable and privacy-sensitive feature toggles where AI is available. • Reminder cadence, quiet hours, timezone; notifications only after opt-in. • Reset lesson/module/language progress; export; delete account. • Switching target language does not erase progress/mastery/review/collections of other language.

• Content-driven: structured content/schema separate from rendering code. • Modular monolith first + workers for long/cost-heavy jobs; microservices only after measured need. • Provider-neutral: image, TTS, STT, AI, email/push, storage via adapters/internal contracts. • Language-scoped by design in schema, storage, cache keys, analytics and tests. • Version everything that affects learning: content, assets, schema, mastery/scheduler, prompt/style guide, pronunciation lexicon, AI policy. • Privacy/accessibility by design, not end-of-project patches. • Private source control: code/config/schemas/scripts in private Git repository; no secrets in repository. • Hosting is replaceable infrastructure; domain model/contracts must not depend on a specific free hosting vendor.

• Product metrics: lesson completion, review return, due backlog, retention, hint/reveal rate, mastery gain, speech fallback, AI optional-use/fallback. • Content quality: ambiguity/error by item, unexpected valid alternatives, drop-off, media failures, AI suggestion acceptance/rejection. • Analytics never mutates progress and may be unavailable without blocking lesson. 29. speech_job lifecycle created -> uploaded -> queued -> processing -> succeeded | unavailable | failed | cancelled | expired.
